title: Construction of a torsion-controlled coherent algebraization
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, J a quasi-coherent ideal, H a coherent module, N a coherent formal module, and delta:N\to\widehat H_J [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For every affine open U assume that the actual inverse limit of section maps delta_U has kernel and cokernel annihilated by (J(U))^t for some t\ge1, which may depend on U. Then there exist a coherent module F, a map a:F\to H, and beta:N\simeq\widehat F_J such that delta=\widehat a_J\circ beta, and the actual coherent kernel and cokernel of a are both annihilated by one positive power of J. There is no uniqueness assertion in this statement.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover. Restriction and the affine equivalence identify the formal source with a finite completed module Q and the target with the completion of the finite module P of sections of H. The hypothesis supplies ideal-power annihilation of kernel and cokernel of this actual limit map.
The Noetherian completion ring is flat, has the same quotient modulo I, and completion of a finite module is tensor product with that ring. Since I is finitely generated, formal gluing applies.

Apply formal-gluing isogeny to obtain psi:T to P and its compatible completed isomorphism. Its kernel and cokernel comparison isomorphisms transfer the local annihilating exponent. The localizations T_f identify with P_f, and the completion is Q, so the formal-gluing finiteness criterion makes T finite. Tilde gives a coherent local triple with actual torsion kernel and cokernel.

On overlaps lift the completed comparisons between the local triples in both directions. Unique lifts make the composites identities and ensure the cocycle. This is uniqueness of morphism lifts, not uniqueness asserted for arbitrary algebraizations.

proof.text: Glue the local sources, their maps to H, and the termwise formal comparisons. Coherence is local. Take a positive upper bound for the finitely many annihilating exponents (1 for the empty cover); higher ideal powers are contained in lower ones, so it annihilates the actual global kernel and cokernel. The comparison equation holds locally and hence globally.

theorem torsionControlled_algebraization_construction
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J)
    (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H)
    (hlocal : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
      J.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) (LinearMap.ker
        (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight δ.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom) ∧
      J.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1)
        (↥(limit (((completion X J).obj H).obj ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)) :
          ModuleCat Γ(X, U.1)) ⧸ LinearMap.range
          (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight δ.hom
            (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom)) :
    ∃ (F : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H) (β : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F),
      δ = β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a ∧
      (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (kernel a.hom)) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (cokernel a.hom)))
